newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile blue chips surge to close up 2.25 percent.
newsitem.headline: Chile blue chips surge to close up 2.25 percent.

text.p: Chilean shares stormed higher on Tuesday to close at their strongest this year, with prices propelled by local and foreign buy orders, dealers said.
After the rally, the bourse could suffer a technical adjustment at the opening on Wednesday, though the undertone remains strong, one dealer said.
"We may see some profit-taking in the morning, but the market should pick up as there are still buyers in the U.S." a trader said.
The selective index ended unofficially 2.25 percent higher at 118.43 points.
The general index firmed 1.31 percent to 5,443.26 points in heavy volume of 18.8 billion pesos.
Local investors swarmed back into the market after they realized that figures showing stronger-than-expected economic growth in December were the result of one-time factors, traders said.
"People reacted positively to the fact that GDP growth in December was largely explainable," said one dealer.
The market had feared that any signs of a surge in growth would prevent the central bank from making a widely expected cut in interest rates next month, dealers said.
Foreign buying boosted most Latin American bolsas, although Chilean stocks outpaced other markets in the region including Sao Paulo and Mexico City.
Gainers included copper products maker Madeco, up 4.24 percent at 1,230 pesos, power utility Enersis, up 3.17 percent at 277 pesos, and telecom CTC which climbed 3.09 percent at 3,000 pesos.
Losers included telecom Entel, down 0.17 percent at 2,920 pesos and pension fund manager Provida which lost 0.01 percent at 9,599 pesos.
